title: The tax answers nobody could check
scenario:
You are a knowledge manager at an accounting firm. Staff use an internal assistant to answer tax questions from the firm's memos. The memos are passed to the model as search results with citations turned on.

A senior advisor audited a sample of answers last week. The managing partner asks you what to change. The exhibit shows the audit.
exhibit:
Tax helpdesk assistant: citation audit (made-up example data)

Sample: 50 answers from last week, checked by a senior advisor
  Cited passage supports the claim                41
  Cited passage exists, but doesn't support it      6
  No citation at all                                3

User interface today: citations hidden; staff see only the answer

Project sponsor's proposed goal:
  "Zero unsupported answers by next month."

Planned feature: web search on public tax-authority websites

questions.prompt: What does the audit tell you about citations?

options.text: The feature is broken: 6 of the citations point to text that cannot be found in the memos.
options.explanation: The exhibit says those passages exist. The pointers are valid; the problem is that the text doesn't support the claim.

options.text: A valid pointer is not proof: in 6 of 50 answers the passage didn't support the claim.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's citations page guarantees valid pointers to your documents, but whether the passage supports the claim still needs checking.

options.text: The assistant is reliable enough, because 47 of the 50 answers came with a citation.
options.explanation: Having a citation is not the same as being supported. Only 41 of 50 answers were backed by their passage.

options.text: The team should turn citations off, because each citation adds output token cost.
options.explanation: Anthropic's citations page says cited_text doesn't count toward output tokens; input tokens rise only slightly. Turning citations off removes the check.

questions.prompt: Staff can't see citations today. What should the interface do?

options.text: Keep them hidden, so that staff read the answers faster and don't get distracted by links.
options.explanation: Hidden citations can't be checked. Staff would have to trust every answer, including the 9 weak ones.

options.text: Show one list of all the memos searched, at the bottom of each answer.
options.explanation: A list at the bottom doesn't show which memo backs which claim. Staff can't check a single claim quickly.

options.text: Show citations only after a staff member reports an answer as wrong.
options.explanation: Staff can't spot a wrong answer without the source. The citation should be there before they act.

options.text: Show each citation next to its claim, with the memo title and a link to the passage.
options.explanation: Right. Then staff can check any claim in one click. Search result blocks carry the source and title you provide.

questions.prompt: How should you respond to the sponsor's goal?

options.text: Set a measured target, audit 50 answers weekly, and send high-stakes answers to an advisor.
options.explanation: Right. Anthropic's guide says these techniques reduce hallucinations but don't remove them, so measure and keep people on critical answers.

options.text: Accept it: with citations turned on, every claim in every answer is guaranteed to be supported.
options.explanation: The guarantee is about valid pointers, not support. The audit already found 6 unsupported claims with valid pointers.

options.text: Accept it, and add "only make supported claims" to the prompt to reach zero.
options.explanation: An instruction can help, but Anthropic's guide says these techniques don't remove hallucinations. Zero is not a realistic target.

options.text: Stop the assistant: if any answer is unsupported, staff can't use it for work.
options.explanation: 41 of 50 answers were supported and checkable. The better path is to measure, improve and keep people on high-stakes answers.

questions.prompt: For the planned web search feature, what must the interface do?

options.text: Nothing new: show web answers in the same way as the memo answers today.
options.explanation: Today the citations are hidden. Both vendors' web search docs say citations must be shown to end users.

options.text: Show citations only for answers that include a number or a tax rate.
options.explanation: The vendor rules cover displayed web results in general, not only numbers.

options.text: Show the web sources as visible citations with the answer, as both vendors require.
options.explanation: Right. The OpenAI docs say inline citations must be clearly visible and clickable; the Claude docs say citations to the original source must be included.

options.text: Hide the web citations, because public pages are less trusted than the firm's own memos.
options.explanation: Both vendors' docs require citations when web results are shown to end users, and staff need them to check the source.
